name: Teaching Methodology Framework
description: A lesson-planning study guide based on John Connors and Jon Grayzel’s public article about teaching BJJ.
summary: Audit a lesson’s purpose, explanation and understanding checks with a published BJJ teaching format.
overview: A demonstration can show a movement without making its purpose clear. John Connors and Jon Grayzel describe a four-part presentation format and prompted recall in Teaching BJJ to Kids. The article says the presentation format is also used in adult classes. This guide uses that example to inspect lesson design.

fits: You explain techniques and want to check whether students understand the problem each lesson addresses.
consider_alternative_if: For planning your own position study, use Blue to Purple Progression; this page concerns presenting a lesson to other people.

includes: A presentation format separating purpose, identification and execution from students applying the technique with gradually increasing resistance.
Recall prompts with hints when a student struggles.
limits: One instructor’s account does not establish a universal curriculum or a ranking of teaching methods.
The article does not supply promotion criteria or a certification process for instructors.

start_here.title: Audit a lesson you already teach
start_here.task: Read the presentation and recall paragraphs. Take notes from one of your own lessons and label where you explain the purpose, identify the technique, describe execution and give students an opportunity to apply it. The article’s “What If?” phase is partner application with gradually increasing resistance. Inspect how your notes distinguish demonstration from student practice; identify an unclear practice objective without adding a drill. Draft a recall prompt and a helpful hint.

sources.title: Teaching BJJ to Kids — John Connors and Jon Grayzel
sources.note: Read the guest article and its four-part presentation format, prompted recall and positional practice description. It reports the authors’ teaching approach, rather than a comparison proving one method best.
sources.viewed_range: Article text, especially the Why/What/How/What If and Active Recall paragraphs

flashcards.question: In Connors and Grayzel’s BJJ lesson format, what does the “Why?” explanation establish?
flashcards.answer: It establishes why learning the technique matters before the instructor explains its execution.

flashcards.question: In Connors and Grayzel’s recall method, how does the instructor respond when a student struggles?
flashcards.answer: The instructor supplies hints or the answer instead of leaving the student stuck.
flashcards.answer_line: Offer a hint or the answer
